blocks.value: **Forgetting to update the control variable.** The most common infinite loop there is.
**Off-by-one errors.** `<` and `<=` differ by one full iteration:

for (int i = 1; i < 10; i++)    // runs 9 times: 1..9
for (int i = 1; i <= 10; i++)   // runs 10 times: 1..10
for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++)    // runs 10 times: 0..9
The last form is the standard one for arrays, where indexes start at `0`.

for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++);      // ← empty body, loops 5 times doing nothing
{ System.out.println(i); }        // runs once, and does not compile. I is out of scope
**Missing the semicolon after `do...while`.** `} while (x < 5)` without `;` will not compile.
**Modifying the control variable inside the body of a `for` loop.** It fights the update expression and produces behaviour nobody can predict by reading.
**Using `continue` in a `while` loop whose update sits at the bottom.** Skips the update, loops forever.
**Expecting `break` to exit all nested loops.** It exits one level only.
**Declaring the control variable inside the loop when you need it afterwards.** `for (int i = ...)` ends `i`'s life with the loop. Declare it before the loop if you need the final value.
